Visible by handle until %1$s. Older app versions and anyone who knows your handle can find you; every such window can be linked to the others.
Turn on rotating discovery IDs first. Without them this phone is always visible by handle.

Off by default. While you are ready for calls, this phone broadcasts a new random ID every 15 minutes instead of its fixed ID, so a scanner cannot follow it from place to place. Other phones see \"Nearby phone\" and learn who you are only when they connect; anyone who connects still learns that. While it is on, this phone\'s Bluetooth name is set to \"Phone\" (your name comes back when you turn it off). Older versions of the app cannot see this phone. Streams, viewers and relays still use the fixed ID for now. Phones paired with this one in Android settings can always recognise it. Takes effect the next time this phone gets ready for calls.
Ask the other person to open Call on their phone. Stay within about 10 to 30 metres. The list updates by itself.

Live video travels encrypted between phones, so only phones watching it can see it. Anyone watching can see it, including phones that pass it on.\n\nFrom: %1$s
Nearby phones can call you while the app is open
When you watch, your phone can pass the video on to phones that are too far from the person who is live. Like you, they can see it. Pauses below 20%% battery or in Battery Saver.
Not live. Tap the red button to start.
Sharing with phones near you, battery %1$d%%
The camera is in use by your call. Compare the safety code above instead, or scan their code from Settings > Verify a contact right after the call.
%1$s. %2$s. Tap to verify who you are talking to.
This phone\'s identity is different from the one you verified for this person. Someone may be pretending to be them. Do not share anything sensitive. End the call and check in person.
Your ID is made from your phone\'s secret key and never leaves it in readable form. To be sure you are talking to the right person, meet once and compare IDs or scan each other\'s code.
Your ID is created the first time you use Bluetooth.
Shows heat and battery temperature. Overheating protection stays on when hidden.
Ease off when the phone gets hot
Hot: 10% less frame rate and quality. Very hot: 20% less. If the phone becomes dangerously hot, video stops even when this is off.
Erases your identity, contacts, messages and settings from this phone. This cannot be undone.
Your identity, verified contacts, messages and settings will be erased now. Other people will see you as a new, unverified person. This cannot be undone.
Quick wipe: triple-tap the app name
Off by default. When on, tapping the app name on the home screen three times quickly starts an emergency wipe after a 3-second chance to undo. Use only if you may need to erase fast.
Connection type, video quality and experiments
Advanced settings. Tap to show or hide.
Helps absorb uneven Bluetooth delivery. It does not change picture quality.
Turn on Manual settings above to change experimental features.
Talk and share video without internet
This app connects phones directly over Bluetooth. It works where there is no mobile signal or Wi-Fi, or where the internet is blocked.
Voice and video calls with people nearby, encrypted from end to end.
Go live for everyone nearby, or watch someone else.

Other phones can carry calls and live video further. A phone that passes on a private call cannot see or hear it. Live video is different: anyone watching it, including a phone that passes it on, can see it.

• No account, no servers, no internet, no analytics.
• Range is about 10 to 30 metres between two phones, less through walls and bodies. Each phone that relays adds another hop.
• Video is small and may pause on a weak link; sound is kept going first.
• Both phones need this app open.
• Tip: before you rely on it, test the range with a friend by walking apart during a call.
Nearby devices: find and connect to other phones.
Location: older Android versions require it for Bluetooth scanning. The app does not read your location.
Camera: video calls and going live. Only while you use them.
Notifications: show incoming calls and ongoing video.
Some access was not allowed. You can allow it later from the home screen.

This app works without internet and never contacts a server.

%1$d setting may stop calls or shared video in the background
Android may pause the app in the background, which can drop calls and shared video. Allow it to run without battery restrictions.
Creates a short technical report (app version, phone model, Bluetooth support). It contains no video, sound, messages, names or keys. You choose where to send it; it is also copied.
No app can open the bug report page. Open the project page on a phone with internet.

Off by default. Adds an optional name (Settings, Your ID), a subject when you place a call and a title when you go live. Names and subjects travel only inside the encrypted call, signed by your identity key; a stream title is also advertised publicly so people nearby see it before joining (shown as unconfirmed until they join). Phones without this see only your handle.
Shown to people you call, marked self-named; your handle never changes. Anyone who knows your handle can tell when your phone is nearby with a Bluetooth scanner.
This name cannot be used (%1$s). Use up to 32 bytes, one script, no handle-like text or check marks.
Public: anyone nearby can read it
Share app nearby is an experimental feature. Turn it on in Advanced settings first.
This needs permission to use nearby Wi-Fi devices.
Without the nearby Wi-Fi permission this phone cannot start a Wi-Fi Direct network, so the app cannot be shared this way. You can still use Share this app.
This phone does not support Wi-Fi Direct.
Turn on Wi-Fi first. No internet or router is needed; the other phone joins this phone directly.
On this Android version, Wi-Fi Direct needs Location turned on. Turn it on, then come back.

Sharing. On the other phone, scan the first code with the camera to join the Wi-Fi network, then scan the second code to open the download page. Keep this screen open.

Sharing on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, which slows Bluetooth on this phone while it lasts. On the other phone, scan the first code to join the Wi-Fi network, then the second code to open the download page. Keep this screen open.
